description: Grouped lollipop chart of pet ownership for eight Australian household groups, each drawn from the national rate of 73%, Animal Medicines Australia survey 2025.

title.description: The big heading and the smaller line under it. On a phone the words are split into shorter lines.

text.signal: narrow ? ['Families and mortgage holders', 'are likeliest to own pets'] : 'Families and mortgage holders are likeliest to own pets'

subtitle.signal: narrow ? ['Share of households owning at least one pet,', 'by household group, 2025'] : 'Share of households owning at least one pet, by household group, 2025'

usermeta.readMe: Vega ignores this box. It holds plain-language notes for the parts of the chart that cannot carry their own "description".

scales.x: Turns a percentage into a left-to-right position, from 50% to 92% (to 97% on a phone, to leave room for labels).

usermeta.codeGuide: Signals set the responsive layout and theme. Data transforms derive values; scales map them to positions and colours; marks draw the chart.
usermeta.readingNote: Household circumstances may shape the feasibility of pet care. These comparisons cannot establish what causes ownership.

signals.name: colorNeutral
signals.description: Colour: the main brown colour, used for plain bars, lines and dots. This is only a backup; the real colour comes from --color-neutral in css/style.css.

signals.name: colorAccent
signals.description: Colour: the blue highlight colour, used for the one thing we want you to notice. This is only a backup; the real colour comes from --color-accent in css/style.css.

signals.name: colorMuted
signals.description: Colour: the dark grey colour of small text: labels, axis words and notes. This is only a backup; the real colour comes from --color-muted in css/style.css.

signals.name: colorHeading
signals.description: Colour: the dark blue colour of chart titles. This is only a backup; the real colour comes from --color-heading in css/style.css.

signals.name: fontHeading
signals.description: Font: the fancy title font (DM Serif Display). This is only a backup; the real font comes from --font-heading in css/style.css.

signals.name: fontBody
signals.description: Font: the plain font for all other text (Fira Sans). This is only a backup; the real font comes from --font-body in css/style.css.

signals.name: width
signals.description: How wide the chart is. It starts as the width of the box on the page and updates whenever the browser window is resized.

signals.name: narrow
signals.description: True below 640 pixels of available width. Group names move above the benchmark dots; wider charts keep a 300-pixel label column.

signals.name: nationalRate
signals.description: The share of all Australian homes with a pet: 73%. Every lollipop starts from here.

signals.name: highlight
signals.description: Which comparison is coloured blue to match the note: "Household" (household make-up).

signals.name: labelWidth
signals.description: How much room is kept on the left for group names: 300 pixels on a computer, none on a phone (names go above each lollipop).

signals.name: headerHeight
signals.description: Room above each comparison block for its heading.

signals.name: rowHeight
signals.description: How tall each group row is: taller on a phone to fit the name above the lollipop.

signals.name: blockGap
signals.description: Extra space between two comparison blocks.

signals.name: blockHeight
signals.description: How tall one comparison block is: its heading, two group rows and the gap.

signals.name: plotHeight
signals.description: How tall the area with the lollipops is: four blocks.

signals.name: height
signals.description: Plot and axis only; the reading note wraps in HTML below the SVG.

data.name: groups
data.description: The survey numbers: for each household group (for example "Apartments or units"), the share of homes with a pet.

transform.description: Copy the percentage into a shorter field name, "pct".
Replace short group names from the file with full words, for example "Families with children at home".
transform.expr: {'Apartment/unit': 'Apartments or units', 'Own outright': 'Own their home outright', 'Families with kids at home': 'Families with children at home', 'Living alone/couples without kids': 'Living alone or couples without children', 'At least AUD 100000 annually': '$100,000 or more a year', 'Below AUD 50000 annually': 'Under $50,000 a year'}[datum.group] || datum.group

transform.description: Write each comparison's heading in full words, for example "Type of home".
Give each comparison its block number, 0 to 3, from top to bottom.
Inside each comparison, number the groups 1 and 2, with the higher percentage first.
Work out how far each group is above or below the national rate.
Mark the groups in the highlighted comparison, so they can be coloured blue.

data.name: blocks
data.description: One row per comparison (type of home, home ownership, household make-up, household income), used for the headings.

marks.description: The box that holds the lollipops, headings, national rate line and axis.

axes.description: The bottom axis: share of homes owning at least one pet, in percent.
axes.title: Households owning at least one pet

marks.description: On a computer: one dashed upright line at the national rate (73%), running the full height. Hidden on a phone.
On a phone: short dashed pieces of the national rate line, only beside each lollipop, so the line never crosses the group names. Hidden on a computer.
The words "National rate 73%" at the top of the dashed line.
The comparison headings, for example "Type of home". The highlighted one is blue.
The group names: in a left column on a computer, above each lollipop on a phone. Its height is worked out from its comparison block and whether it is the first or second group in that block.

tooltip.signal: {'Comparison': datum.dimension_label, 'Household group': datum.label, 'Households owning pets': format(datum.pct, ',') + '%', 'National ownership rate': nationalRate + '%', 'Difference from national rate': format(abs(datum.difference), ',') + ' percentage points ' + (datum.difference > 0 ? 'above' : datum.difference < 0 ? 'below' : 'equal to') , 'Value basis': datum.derivation === 'reported' ? 'Published ownership percentage' : 'Calculated from the published non-owner percentage'}
